title: Vulvar Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 clinical navigator for Vulvar Cancer. Covers complete clinical algorithm: Diagnostic Workup (thorough vulvar, perineal, and perianal inspection with bilateral inguinofemoral nodal palpation and colposcopy, full-thickness punch or wedge biopsy to deep subcutaneous fat for depth of stromal invasion, histopathology of SCC HPV-associated vs HPV-independent dVIN TP53-mutant vs adenocarcinoma vs melanoma, pelvic and groin MRI or CT with contrast, whole-body FDG-PET/CT for locally advanced or node-suspicious cases, biomarker testing for p16/HPV, TP53, PD-L1 CPS, and MMR/MSI) -> FIGO Stage Stratification (Stage IA microinvasive vs Stage IB-II localized cN0 vs Stage III-IVa locoregionally advanced node-positive vs Stage IVb distant metastatic) -> Stage IA radical local excision with 1 cm or greater margins and no groin dissection -> Stage IB-II radical local excision with SLNB or inguinofemoral dissection plus adjuvant RT for positive margins, micrometastases, or ENE -> Locoregionally advanced definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (pelvic/groin EBRT with weekly cisplatin, organ-sparing) -> Metastatic first-line systemic chemoimmunotherapy (platinum plus paclitaxel plus pembrolizumab with or without bevacizumab per KEYNOTE-826 extrapolated data; second-line pembrolizumab monotherapy or palliative RT). References StewardMD Standard Protocols. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides and dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Vulvar Cancer Version 2.2026.

a.text: Diagnosis requires full-thickness punch or wedge biopsy extending to deep subcutaneous fat so depth of stromal invasion can be measured accurately; invasion depth of 1.0 mm or less with tumor size 2 cm or less defines microinvasive Stage IA disease with negligible nodal risk.

b.text: Histology is squamous cell carcinoma in over 90% of cases, split into HPV-associated (p16-positive) and HPV-independent (differentiated VIN or lichen sclerosus background, frequently TP53-mutant) pathways; adenocarcinoma (including Bartholin gland) and vulvar melanoma follow separate histology-specific management.

c.text: Sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) with technetium-99m plus blue dye or ICG applies to unifocal tumors under 4 cm with clinically negative groins; lateral tumors over 2 cm from midline qualify for unilateral staging while central or midline tumors require bilateral inguinofemoral staging.

d.text: Postoperative adjuvant radiotherapy (PORT 50-60 Gy) is indicated for positive surgical margins, multiple inguinofemoral micrometastases, or extranodal extension (ENE) after inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy.

e.text: Definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy: EBRT 45-50.4 Gy to elective primary, bilateral inguinofemoral, and pelvic nodal basins with boost of gross disease to 64-70 Gy, plus concurrent weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 IV during EBRT for 5-6 doses (or cisplatin plus 5-FU); this organ-sparing approach avoids upfront pelvic exenteration.

f.text: Metastatic first-line systemic therapy extrapolates KEYNOTE-826 cervical data: carboplatin AUC 5 (or cisplatin 50 mg/m2) plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 plus pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks (or 400 mg every 6 weeks) with or without bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks; second-line pembrolizumab monotherapy applies to PD-L1 CPS 1 or higher, MSI-H, or TMB-H disease, with palliative radiation for symptomatic groin or bone metastases.

nodes.name: Diagnostic Workup
nodes.title: Vulvar Cancer: Diagnostic Workup Checklist
nodes.description: Step 1: Complete the clinical workup before FIGO stage stratification. Inspect and palpate the vulva and groins, confirm stromal invasion depth on full-thickness biopsy, subtype histology and biomarkers, and stage local and distant extent with MRI and PET/CT.
bullets: Thorough vulvar, perineal, and perianal inspection and palpation of bilateral inguinofemoral lymph nodes with colposcopic evaluation
Diagnostic full-thickness punch or wedge biopsy extending to deep subcutaneous fat to accurately measure depth of stromal invasion
Histopathology: squamous cell carcinoma (over 90%; HPV-associated vs HPV-independent dVIN / TP53-mutant), adenocarcinoma, or melanoma
Pelvic and groin MRI with contrast (or CT with IV contrast) to evaluate local tumor invasion and inguinofemoral/pelvic lymphadenopathy
Whole-body FDG-PET/CT for regional nodal metastases and distant screening in locally advanced (Stage II or higher) or suspicious node cases
Biomarker testing on tumor tissue: p16/HPV status, TP53 immunohistochemistry, PD-L1 (CPS), and MMR/MSI

options.label: Workup Complete - Proceed to FIGO Stage Stratification

nodes.name: FIGO Stage Stratification
nodes.title: Vulvar Cancer: FIGO Stage Stratification
nodes.description: Workup complete. Assign FIGO stage from tumor size, depth of stromal invasion, adjacent structure involvement, clinical nodal status, and distant spread; the group selects the microinvasive excision, localized excision plus groin staging, definitive chemoradiotherapy, or metastatic systemic-therapy pathway.
bullets: FIGO Stage IA microinvasive: tumor size 2 cm or less with stromal invasion 1.0 mm or less and clinically negative nodes (cN0).
FIGO Stage IB-II localized: tumor over 2 cm or invasion over 1 mm, including disease involving adjacent perineal structures, with clinically negative nodes (cN0).
Locoregionally advanced / node-positive: Stage III-IVa with fixed or ulcerated inguinofemoral nodes, or involvement of upper urethra, vagina, bladder, or rectal mucosa.
Distant metastatic: FIGO Stage IVb with spread beyond regional nodes to distant organs or non-regional nodes.

options.label: FIGO Stage IA Microinvasive Vulvar Cancer (Tumor size <=2cm and stromal invasion <=1.0mm, cN0)
FIGO Stage IB-II Localized Vulvar Cancer (Size >2cm or invasion >1mm, adjacent structures, cN0)

Distant Metastatic Vulvar Cancer (FIGO Stage IVb)

nodes.name: Stage IA Treatment
nodes.title: Stage IA Microinvasive: Radical Local Excision Without Groin Dissection
nodes.description: Radical local excision with wide macroscopic margins down to deep fascia for microinvasive Stage IA vulvar cancer; groin nodal staging is not required given the negligible risk of nodal metastasis.
bullets: Radical local excision / wide local excision with 1 cm or greater macroscopic margins down to deep fascia for the primary tumor.
Inguinal lymphadenectomy or sentinel lymph node biopsy is NOT required due to negligible risk of nodal metastasis (under 1%) in Stage IA microinvasive disease.
Confirm negative surgical margins on pathology with stromal invasion 1.0 mm or less; re-excise for positive margins.
Postoperative observation with vulvar and inguinofemoral examination; routine adjuvant radiotherapy is not indicated.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
nodes.regimenSummary: Radical Local Excision with >=1cm Margins (No Groin Dissection Required)

nodes.name: Stage IB-II Treatment
nodes.title: Stage IB-II Localized: Radical Excision Plus SLNB or Inguinofemoral Dissection
nodes.description: Radical local excision with inguinofemoral nodal staging for localized Stage IB-II vulvar cancer: sentinel lymph node biopsy for small unifocal cN0 tumors, or unilateral or bilateral inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy by laterality, with adjuvant radiotherapy for high-risk pathology.
bullets: Radical local excision of the primary tumor with 1 cm or greater macroscopic margins down to deep fascia.
Inguinofemoral nodal staging: sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB using technetium-99m and blue dye/ICG) for unifocal tumors under 4 cm with clinically negative groins.
Unilateral inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy (ILND) for lateral tumors over 2 cm from midline, or bilateral ILND for central/midline tumors, when SLNB criteria are not met or SLNB is positive.
Postoperative adjuvant radiotherapy (PORT 50-60 Gy) for positive margins, multiple micrometastases, or extranodal extension (ENE).
Surveillance after definitive therapy: vulvar, groin, and pelvic examination with cross-sectional imaging for symptoms or high-risk pathology.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
nodes.regimenSummary: Radical Local Excision + Sentinel Lymph Node Biopsy (SLNB) or Inguinofemoral Dissection

nodes.name: Locoregionally Advanced Treatment
nodes.title: Stage III-IVa: Definitive Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy (Organ-Sparing)
nodes.description: Definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy for locoregionally advanced or node-positive vulvar cancer: pelvic and groin EBRT with concurrent weekly cisplatin as an organ-sparing approach that avoids upfront pelvic exenteration.
bullets: Definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy: primary tumor plus bilateral inguinofemoral and pelvic lymph node basins treated with external beam radiotherapy (EBRT: 45-50.4 Gy to elective nodal basins, boost gross disease to 64-70 Gy).
Concurrent weekly cisplatin (40 mg/m2 IV weekly during EBRT x 5-6 cycles) or cisplatin plus 5-FU selected by fitness, renal function, and hearing status.
Organ-sparing approach avoiding upfront pelvic exenteration; reassess for limited surgical resection of residual disease after chemoradiotherapy.
Monitor renal function, audiologic status, hematologic counts, and skin toxicity during concurrent chemoradiotherapy; coordinate across gynecologic oncology, medical oncology, and radiation oncology.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
nodes.regimenSummary: Definitive Concurrent ChemoRT (Pelvic/Groin EBRT + Weekly Cisplatin 40 mg/m2)

nodes.name: Metastatic Treatment
nodes.title: Stage IVb: First-Line Systemic Chemoimmunotherapy Then Pembrolizumab
nodes.description: First-line platinum, paclitaxel, and pembrolizumab with or without bevacizumab for distant metastatic vulvar cancer, followed by pembrolizumab monotherapy for biomarker-selected disease or palliative radiation for symptomatic metastases.
bullets: First-line systemic chemoimmunotherapy: carboplatin (AUC 5) or cisplatin (50 mg/m2) plus paclitaxel (175 mg/m2) plus pembrolizumab (200 mg IV q3w or 400 mg q6w) with or without bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV q3w (KEYNOTE-826 data extrapolated).
Second-line: pembrolizumab monotherapy (for PD-L1 CPS 1 or higher, MSI-H, or TMB-H) with immune-related adverse event monitoring.
Palliative radiation for symptomatic groin or bone metastases for pain control and local symptom relief.
Establish PD-L1 CPS, MMR/MSI, TMB, p16/HPV, and TP53 status at diagnosis of metastatic disease to set immunotherapy eligibility; offer clinical trial enrollment at every line.
Stage with cross-sectional imaging at baseline and every 8-12 weeks on systemic therapy.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
